subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: Which public web-tool egress boundary should OpenClaw support for this request: a scoped web_fetch hostname allowlist first, a managed-proxy policy boundary, or a cross-tool search/fetch/browser allow/deny policy?
rationale: This adds an operator-trusted security/config surface, and the current related PRs encode different answers that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve scoped web_fetch allowlist first
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step while keeping deny, search, browser, and proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make managed proxy the boundary
options.body: Pause local web_fetch config work and route application-owned egress policy through the managed proxy direction instead.

options.title: Require cross-tool design
options.body: Hold implementation until fetch, search, browser, provider fallback, redirects, caches, and plugin HTTP share one documented policy model.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped web_fetch allowlist first
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step while keeping deny, search, browser, and proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across the SSRF, guarded fetch, and web_fetch runtime surfaces involved in this boundary choice.
